_procedure: Regenerating these numbers: (1) uv run python -m tests.eval.run --all --write-baseline; (2) read tests/eval/baseline/*.report.md and confirm every number is what you expect; (3) uv run python -m tests.eval.run --language en --print-thresholds, then paste its output below with each floor rounded DOWN slightly. Floors sit just under measured, never at an aspirational target: this suite exists to catch a real drop, not to fail on day one. Raise a floor only after a deliberate improvement; lower one only with a note in the commit message explaining why the regression is accepted.
_no_k1_on_retrieval_raw: retrieval_raw has no k=1 block on purpose. The dense stub returns one fixed chunk that ties the top keyword hit on RRF score and wins by insertion order, so rank 1 is always the stub and every k=1 metric there is pinned at 0.0. A floor of 0.0 would be noise. test_pipeline_tripwires.py fails loudly when that stops being true.
_precision_not_thresholded: precision_at_k is reported but never given a floor: with one or two relevant chunks per question its ceiling at k=5 is 0.2-0.4, so a floor would penalise a perfect run.
_refusal_not_thresholded: refusal_rate and correct_refusal_rate are 0.0 today because the dense stub always supplies evidence, so the pipeline can never refuse. A floor of 0.0 is vacuous; these become thresholdable when the vector store is real.
